details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has expressed caution regarding proposals to expand euro stablecoins, warning EU finance ministers that such a move could jeopardize bank lending and the central bank's control over interest rates. This stance aligns with the ECB's preference for tokenized commercial bank deposits over stablecoins to maintain financial stability and monetary sovereignty.
title: ECB Wary of Expanding Euro Stablecoins

details: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that Washington has seized nearly $1 billion worth of Iranian assets held in cryptocurrency. This action is part of an escalating economic campaign aimed at severing Tehran's access to international finance.
title: US Seizes Nearly $1 Billion in Iranian Crypto Assets

details: Bloomberg analysts indicate that Bitcoin's volatility and correlation are increasingly converging with gold. Furthermore, the BlackRock Bitcoin Spot ETF (IBIT) has significantly outperformed US stocks since the escalation of the conflict in Iran, achieving more than double the excess return of the S&P 500 ETF (SPY) since its approval.
title: Bitcoin Volatility Nears Gold Levels, IBIT Outperforms Stocks

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) views tokenization as a structural shift in financial architecture that offers efficiencies but also risks amplifying financial instability. The IMF advocates for wholesale central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) as safe settlement assets within this evolving landscape.
title: IMF Highlights Tokenization's Promise and Perils

details: Crypto investment firm Capriole Investments has issued a warning that every historical instance of inflation reaching current levels (US CPI at 3.8% in April 2026) has been followed by an average market crash of 30% over the subsequent one to 24 months. This elevated inflation poses a macro spillover risk to Bitcoin and the broader crypto market if traditional markets experience a downturn.
title: Persistent Inflation Raises Market Crash Warnings

details: Spot Bitcoin ETFs have experienced a record nine-day outflow streak, totaling $2.84 billion, which is the longest since their launch. Overall cryptocurrency market sentiment remains cautious, with the Fear & Greed Index hovering in the 'fear' zone (around 34 points), despite some social media sentiment showing a bullish lean for Bitcoin. The sustained outflows and prevailing fear suggest that investors are reevaluating digital assets in light of macroeconomic risks and declining risk appetite.
title: Bitcoin ETF Outflows Continue Amid Cautious Sentiment

details: Expectations for higher-for-longer interest rates continue to pressure speculative assets, including cryptocurrencies. The bond market, with US 10-year Treasury yields remaining above 4.4% (one of the highest levels of 2026), continues to attract capital, potentially reducing demand for riskier assets like cryptocurrencies. Skepticism also remains in the market regarding early Federal Reserve rate cuts in 2026.
title: Higher-for-Longer Interest Rates Weigh on Crypto

details: XRP continues to demonstrate growth in cross-border payments, with Ripple's On-Demand Liquidity (ODL) platform processing over $15 billion in 2024. Stellar has secured a significant institutional endorsement, being chosen by DTCC (which oversees $114 trillion in US capital market assets) as the first public blockchain to host its tokenized securities. Additionally, the CLARITY Act, a significant piece of crypto market structure legislation, is anticipated for a Senate floor vote in July 2026, which could provide further regulatory clarity for the crypto market.
sourceName: 24/7 Wall St. (citing various data points for XRP/Stellar)
title: XRP and Stellar Gain Institutional Traction, CLARITY Act Looms
